questions.question: Find the accessibility bug in this table.
questions.explanation: Table headers should use `<th>` instead of `<td><strong>`. This provides semantic meaning for assistive technologies.

questions.question: Find the semantic bug in this navigation.
questions.explanation: The navigation is wrapped in a generic `<div>`. Use the semantic `<nav>` element instead to improve accessibility and SEO.

questions.question: Find the accessibility bug in this form input.
questions.explanation: The input has no `<label>`. Placeholders are not a substitute for labels; they disappear when typing and are not announced correctly by all screen readers.

questions.question: Find the bug that harms accessibility and semantics.
questions.codeSnippet:
Article Title

Some content...

Posted by John on Jan 1
questions.explanation: The article's footer should use the semantic `<footer>` element instead of a `<div>`. This provides a landmark for assistive tech.

questions.question: Find the ARIA misuse in this button.
questions.explanation: A `<div>` with `role="button"` is not a true button. It lacks native keyboard events and browser behaviour. Use `<button>` instead – the first rule of ARIA is don't use ARIA if a native element exists.

questions.question: Find the bug that breaks keyboard accessibility.
questions.explanation: Removing `outline` without providing a custom visible focus indicator makes the button unusable for keyboard-only users.
